topics.label: Birds
facts: Birds have feathers, wings, and beaks.
Most birds can fly, but some, like penguins and ostriches, cannot.
Birds lay eggs, and baby birds hatch from the eggs.
Many birds build nests to keep their eggs safe.

questions.q: What do birds have that helps them fly?
questions.fact: Feathers and wings help most birds fly.
Birds lay eggs, and baby birds hatch out of them.
Penguins cannot fly, but they are great swimmers.

questions.q: Where do many birds keep their eggs safe?
questions.fact: Birds build nests from twigs and grass to protect their eggs.

topics.label: Fish
facts: Fish live in water and breathe using gills.
Fish swim with their fins and tails.
Most fish have scales covering their bodies.
Some fish live in the sea, and some live in rivers and lakes.

questions.fact: Fish live in water, in seas, rivers, and lakes.

questions.q: How do fish breathe under water?
questions.fact: Gills take oxygen out of the water so fish can breathe.

questions.q: What do fish use to swim?
questions.fact: Fish push themselves through water with their fins and tails.
Most fish are covered in shiny scales.

topics.label: Insects
facts: Insects have six legs and three body parts.
Bees, ants, butterflies, and ladybirds are insects.
Bees help flowers by carrying pollen from one flower to another.

questions.q: How many legs does an insect have?
Which of these is an insect?
questions.fact: Bees are insects. Spiders have eight legs, so they are not insects.

questions.q: What does a caterpillar turn into?
questions.fact: A caterpillar changes into a butterfly inside a chrysalis.
When bees visit flowers, pollen sticks to them and helps new seeds grow.

topics.label: Butterflies
facts: A butterfly starts life as a tiny egg, then becomes a caterpillar, then a chrysalis, then a butterfly.
Butterflies taste with their feet, using special sensors on their legs.
A butterfly's wings are covered in tiny scales, like dust, which give them their colours.
Monarch butterflies travel thousands of kilometres every year to reach warmer places.

questions.q: What does a caterpillar turn into inside a chrysalis?
questions.fact: Inside the chrysalis, a caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

questions.q: How do butterflies taste their food?
questions.fact: Butterflies have taste sensors on their feet.

questions.q: What covers a butterfly's wings and gives them colour?
questions.fact: Butterfly wings are covered in tiny coloured scales.

questions.q: Which butterfly travels thousands of kilometres every year?
questions.fact: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of kilometres to warmer places.
